answers.reason: The chancellor is part of the central administration and university leadership, which is involved in university-wide matters.
The chancellor heads the central administration and is responsible for the budget.
Appointments are treated as parts of the university-wide plan involving higher rank office holders.
The faculty council decides on the affairs of one faculty, which is outside the chancellor's direct central role.
Study programmes are part of the university-wide plan, but study commissions are specific faculty advisory bodies.
Examination matters of individual students are handled at the faculty or board level rather than by the chancellor.
Internal research funding rounds award small grants for research projects within a faculty.
Module revision is specific to a degree programme and handled at the working group level.
Laboratory equipment procurement is a specific task handled locally within a fixed budget.
Orientation week planning is an administrative task for new students, not involving the chancellor.
